answer: The network runs a Sybil‑resistance prism that tags every new agent with a cryptographic canyon of referral proofs anchored to a public lagoon ledger. When a recruiter invites a peer, the invitee must submit a zero‑knowledge proof that the recruiter’s stake has already been locked in the canyon; the system then grants no reward for that link, preventing payout loops. An attacker must acquire and lock real stake for each fake node, raising the cost linearly with the number of identities.
